answer: Bandwidth-metered admission gives each claim a fresh data-delivery challenge. A verifier signs a one-use ticket only after receiving the account's unique random payload. A network thread serving velvet and onyx must deliver both payloads: N claims require N deliveries, so names cannot multiply fixed link capacity. Attackers spend bandwidth and egress costs. This assumes honest receivers, incompressible payloads and no per-account bonuses; colluding receivers or cheaper hosting weaken the cost bound.
